title: Database Systems
description: Database systems from the problems of file-based systems to the three-level architecture, entity-relationship and enhanced ER design, the relational model and algebra, SQL, normalization and physical design, and transactions, concurrency control and recovery. Built from the CSC 472 lecture notes and the 2022/23 examination.

topics.title: Introduction to Database Systems
topics.summary: File-based systems suffered from redundancy, isolation, poor sharing and weak security, so database management systems emerged to manage shared, integrated data. The three-level ANSI-SPARC architecture (external, conceptual, internal) gives logical and physical data independence, and a DBMS provides a DDL to define and a DML to query the database.
subtopics: Problems of file-based systems
Data, information, database and DBMS; components of the DBMS environment
History: hierarchical, network, relational and object generations
Advantages and disadvantages of a DBMS
Three-level architecture; logical and physical data independence
Data models; DDL and DML

topics.title: Entity-Relationship Modelling
topics.summary: Conceptual design gathers requirements from stakeholders and models them as entities, attributes and relationships. Attributes are simple or composite, single or multivalued, or derived; relationships have a degree; keys identify entities; and weak entities depend on an owner entity.
subtopics: Requirement gathering and fact finding
Strong and weak entities
Simple, composite, single-valued, multivalued and derived attributes
Relationships, their degree and recursive relationships
Candidate, primary and other keys
Entity or attribute? Entity or relationship?

topics.title: Structural Constraints and Enhanced ER Design
topics.summary: Multiplicity, made up of cardinality and participation, captures business rules on relationships (1:1, 1:*, *:*). Enhanced ER modelling adds superclasses and subclasses with attribute inheritance, specialization and generalization with participation and disjoint constraints, and aggregation; fan and chasm traps are problems to avoid.
subtopics: Attributes on relationships
Multiplicity: cardinality and participation
One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships
Fan traps and chasm traps
Superclasses, subclasses and attribute inheritance
Specialization, generalization, their constraints, and aggregation

topics.title: The Relational Model and Relational Algebra
topics.summary: A relational database is a set of relations, each with a schema and an instance of distinct tuples. Integrity constraints, especially primary and foreign keys, keep instances legal, and referential integrity actions decide what happens on delete. Relational algebra (selection, projection, set operations, cross-product, joins) and relational calculus are the formal query languages behind SQL.
subtopics: Relations: schema, instance, cardinality and degree
Integrity constraints; keys, superkeys and candidate keys
Foreign keys and referential integrity: NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT
Views
Relational algebra: selection, projection, union, difference, cross-product, joins
Tuple and domain relational calculus

topics.title: SQL
topics.summary: SQL defines relations with CREATE TABLE, domain types and constraints, changes data with INSERT, DELETE and UPDATE, and queries it with SELECT-FROM-WHERE. Queries can remove duplicates, rename, nest subqueries with IN, EXISTS and UNIQUE, combine results with set operations, and summarise with aggregate functions, GROUP BY and HAVING.
subtopics: DDL: CREATE TABLE, domain types, NOT NULL and PRIMARY KEY
Insert, delete, update; DROP and ALTER TABLE
SELECT, FROM, WHERE; DISTINCT and rename
Nested and correlated queries: IN, EXISTS, UNIQUE
Set operations: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT
Aggregates, GROUP BY, HAVING and null values

topics.title: Functional Dependencies, Normalization and Physical Design
topics.summary: Redundancy causes update, insertion and deletion anomalies, and functional dependencies identify it. Normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) guide decomposition, which should be lossless and dependency preserving. Physical design then chooses file organizations and indexes, clustered or unclustered, for the important queries.
subtopics: Redundancy and update, insertion and deletion anomalies
Functional dependencies, closure and Armstrong's axioms
First, second and third normal forms
Boyce-Codd normal form
Decomposition
File organizations and indexes: clustered and unclustered

topics.title: Transactions, Concurrency Control and Recovery
topics.summary: A transaction is a unit of work that must be atomic, consistent, isolated and durable (ACID), passing through active, partially committed, committed, failed and aborted states. Concurrency control ensures serializable schedules, through locking (two-phase locking) or timestamps, and recovery uses logs or shadow paging after failures.
subtopics: The ACID properties
Transaction states
Schedules: serial and concurrent
Conflict and view serializability; precedence graphs
Shared and exclusive locks; two-phase locking; deadlock
Timestamp ordering; log-based recovery and shadow paging
